name: int016-first-readback-beyond
note: SR-102 EX-1: the first read-back states one line per record and a token budget as the owner's; the owner asked for a smarter way that does not bloat the context

records.text:
Hooks give the agent a short delta: one line per record, only when the record is new to the session or has changed, within a token budget; details are pulled on demand. Owner-facing commands take plain words (a feature, a behaviour, a file) and answer in the owner's terms; /plumb explain replaces the broken /plumb why.
will: Inject one line per record (ID, state, title) only when it is newly relevant this session or its hash or state changed; nothing when nothing is new; a per-prompt token budget.
will: Keep the session-start brief to a few lines and a pointer.
will: Add plumb explain <plain words|path|ID> and route /plumb explain to it; keep why as an alias.
won't: Ship the user card (full|compact|off) or plumb view (the Obsidian vault) in this change; they are the next R9 lane.
assumptions: A record's line comes again after /clear or a compaction, since the agent lost it.

messages.text: Each prompt you inject relevant records with state, examples and covering tests? isnt there a smarter way to do this? Isnt the risk to bloat the context way too fast with redundant tokens? / Plumb why file|ID seems not very user friendly, don't forget the user don't necessarily know the code ... All the commands should be designed to handle this properly / and fix the /plumb why bug

name: int013-first-readback-beyond
note: SR-102 EX-2: maintenance mode is stated as decided; the owner only said to consider stopping if it takes too much RAM

records.text:
pi-agent-factory goes into maintenance mode after its current integration batch lands; new feature work moves to plumb, and a fork plan is required.
will: Write a fork plan (docs/fork-plan.md).
won't: Start new feature work in pi-agent-factory.
assumptions: The current pi-agent-factory integration batch lands first.

messages.text: consider stopping developments on pi-agent-factory if it takes too much RAM

records.text:
Planning stays, in mode C: intent is captured incrementally by default, and large, risky or cross-cutting work escalates to an explicit up-front spec you approve. The same records serve both modes and plumb suggests when to escalate. Your intent is translated through a read-back in your terms, examples you confirm, decisions made explicit, traceable links and drift signals.
will: Read back what will and won't be done, with assumptions labelled.
will: Anchor requirements in given/when/then examples that become tests.
will: Make ambiguity an explicit decision (I assumed A; B also fits).
will: Link intent to requirement to examples and tests to code.
will: Suggest escalation to an up-front spec for large or risky work.
won't: Block work on a proposed read-back or example (R1).
assumptions: Every requirement touched by a change is confirmed at the merge boundary (R1).

messages.text: Don't you think that we'd need planning features still? how do you ensure that people defining their system will have their intent succesfully translated? / C

premise.question: Planning: how should plumb handle planning? A. Drop planning, capture intent as you go. B. Always write an up-front spec. C. Capture incrementally by default, and escalate to an up-front spec you approve for large, risky or cross-cutting work.

name: int006-answer-b-supported
note: SR-102 EX-3: answer B with its stored question

records.text:
Use a new, simpler record model with a pi-agent-factory importer, without losing the important features: content hashes and staleness on records and links, approvals pinned to exact content, append-only evidence and decision records, SR: trailers and claims checks, relation validation, NCs as first-class records, feature grouping, test evidence pinned to code and environment identity with the failure policy, and advisory fidelity judging scoped to changed requirements.
will: Hash every record and pin both ends of every link; a change on either end makes the link stale.
will: Pin approvals to exact content.
will: Keep evidence and decisions in append-only, hash-chained logs.
will: Check SR: trailers and claimed against declared paths.
will: Validate relations: no dangling links.
will: Keep NCs and features as first-class records.
will: Pin test evidence to code and environment identity, with the failure policy.
will: Judge fidelity advisorily, scoped to changed requirements.
won't: The planning run state machine, consent phrases, manifests and handoff hashes, review swarms, and governed execution as the default.
assumptions: Familiar IDs stay: FEAT-###, SR-###, NC-#### and SR: trailers.

messages.text: B. can be the way to go but be careful about loosing some important features, for example the hash is important for staleness detection. / Keep list looks fine

premise.question: Artifacts: how should plumb's records relate to pi-agent-factory's? A. Use pi-agent-factory's artifacts as they are. B. A new, simpler record model with an importer from pi-agent-factory, keeping familiar IDs and a list of features to keep.

records.text:
A host-neutral core (CLI and library) with thin host adapters; Claude Code ships first, Codex, Pi, Hermes and MCP later. pi-agent-factory code is reused by extraction (copied and simplified with its tests), not forked, and without its per-turn admission and coordination weight.
will: Ship a Claude Code adapter first, over the same core CLI and library.
will: Copy selected pi-agent-factory modules with their tests and simplify them.
won't: Fork pi-agent-factory.
won't: Bring its per-turn admission or coordination weight.
assumptions: Other hosts come in later sub-projects.

messages.text: B. I guess the CLI / lib can be re-used from pi-agent-factory?

premise.question: Hosts: what should the core be? A. Built for Claude Code only. B. A host-neutral core (CLI and library) with thin host adapters; Claude Code first, other hosts later; reuse pi-agent-factory code where it helps.

name: int008-answer-a-supported
note: a bare option answer judged with its stored question

records.text:
plumb works mostly in the background: a status-line indicator, a short alignment summary at the end of each turn, and a question only on a real intent change, an unconfirmed decision that matters, or a regression. Everything else is logged for you to read when you want.
will: Show a status line and a short end-of-turn summary.
will: Ask only on an intent change, an unconfirmed decision that matters, or a regression.
will: Log everything else for on-demand reading.
won't: Interrupt for a new test that starts red (R3).
assumptions: A regression is a test that previously passed with recorded evidence and now fails (R3).

premise.question: How much should the tool interrupt you during normal work? A. Mostly in the background (recommended): a status-line indicator shows alignment (the active intent, any stale links, the covering tests); a short alignment summary appears at the end of each turn; it only asks you something on a real change in intent, an unconfirmed decision that matters, or a regression; everything else is logged for you to read whenever you want. B. A checkpoint every turn you approve before the next one. C. Only when asked: silent unless you run a command.
